title: Finite type of the next matching algebra of an algebraic hypercover truncation
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $B$ be a commutative finite type $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and let $n\geq0$. Let $P$ be an $n$-truncated simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-coskeleton] in the category of commutative $A$-algebras augmented to $B$, with $P_k$ of finite type over $A$ for $0\leq k\leq n$. Define $M_0(P)=B$, $M_1(P)=P_0\times_B P_0$, and, for $2\leq k\leq n+1$, let $M_k(P)$ be the $A$-algebra of tuples $(p_0,\ldots,p_k)\in P_{k-1}^{k+1}$ with $d_i p_j=d_{j-1}p_i$ for $i<j$; all tuple operations are componentwise. Equivalently these are compatible proper-face families over a common element of $B$; that element is forced by the tuple for $k\geq1$. For $1\leq k\leq n$ let $\mu_k:P_k\to M_k(P)$ be $p\mapsto(d_0p,\ldots,d_kp)$, and let $\mu_0:P_0\to B$ be the augmentation. Suppose every $\mu_k$ for $0\leq k\leq n$ is surjective. Then $M_{n+1}(P)$ is of finite type over $A$.

source.place: Tag 08PW (lemma-polynomial), finite type of the next coskeletal term; equivalently the relative matching algebra of a truncation with surjective lower matching maps. The matching formula is made explicit as in the proof; more-algebra.tex lemma-formal-consequence is its finite-type input.

proof.text: Write $P(\alpha):P_t\to P_r$ for the map of an order-preserving $\alpha:[r]\to[t]$. For $0\le k\le n$ and $m\ge k$, form $C_{k,m}$ from a common $b\in B$ and elements $x_\theta\in P_r$ for every $0\le r\le k$ and $\theta:[r]\to[m]$, satisfying $x_{\theta\alpha}=P(\alpha)(x_\theta)$ whenever both dimensions are at most $k$, and augmentation $x_\theta\mapsto b$. Operations are componentwise. Put $C_{-1,m}=B$. These are finite families with finitely many equations. Evaluation at the identity gives $C_{k,k}\cong P_k$, with inverse $p\mapsto(P(\theta)p)_\theta$.

source.place: Tag 08PW (lemma-polynomial), proof: compatible families on skeleta and the cartesian square for successive skeleta.

proof.text: For $1\le k\le n+1$, identify $C_{k-1,k}$ with $M_k(P)$: restriction to the $k+1$ facets gives the tuple of the statement; two facets meet in the face whose two descriptions are $d_i p_j=d_{j-1}p_i$. All lower injective faces lie in a facet, and these pairwise intersection equations make their values independent of the facet chosen. Every order-preserving map uniquely factors as a surjection onto its image followed by that image inclusion, so values on noninjective faces are forced by the degeneracy maps. The functor identities give all compatibility equations. For $k=1$ the common $b$ imposes exactly the fibre-product condition. For $k\ge2$, any two vertices share an edge, so their augmentations agree; every facet has that same augmentation. Thus no extra $b$ remains. Also $C_{-1,0}=M_0(P)=B$.

source.place: Tag 08PW (lemma-polynomial), proof: compatible families on skeleta and the cartesian square for successive skeleta.

proof.text: Fix $0\le k\le n$ and $k<m\le n+1$. Index the injective $k$-faces by $E:[k]\hookrightarrow[m]$. Restriction $\psi_E:C_{k-1,m}\to C_{k-1,k}=M_k(P)$ is surjective. For $k=0$ this is $\mathrm{id}_B$. For $k\ge1$, write $e_j=E(j)$ and put $\rho(t)=\max(\{0\}\cup\{j:e_j\le t\})$. This is order-preserving and $\rho E=\mathrm{id}$. Given a compatible family $y$ on $[k]$, set $x_\theta=y_{\rho\theta}$ and keep its augmentation. This defines a compatible family on $[m]$, since precomposition commutes with every $P(\alpha)$, and its restriction along $E$ is $y$. It is an $A$-algebra section of $\psi_E$.

source.place: Tag 08PW (lemma-polynomial), proof: compatible families on skeleta and the cartesian square for successive skeleta.

proof.text: For these $k,m$ there is a cartesian identification $C_{k,m}\cong C_{k-1,m}\times_{\prod_E M_k(P)}\prod_E P_k$, with maps $(\psi_E)_E$ and $(\mu_k)_E$. Indeed, a full family restricts to a lower family and values $p_E$ on the injective $k$-faces, with boundary $\mu_k(p_E)=\psi_E(x)$. Conversely those boundary equations supply every compatibility with proper subfaces of $E$; all remaining $k$-simplices are degeneracies of lower-dimensional injective faces, with values forced by the surjection--injection factorization. Their compatibility follows by factoring compositions and using the functor identities. Different injective $k$-faces intersect only in dimension less than $k$, so there are no further equations. The two constructions are inverse and preserve componentwise operations. This also proves the case $k=0$: vertices are independent over the common $b$.

source.place: Tag 08PW (lemma-polynomial), proof: compatible families on skeleta and the cartesian square for successive skeleta.

proof.text: Induct on $k$ from $-1$ to $n$ to prove that every $C_{k,m}$, $\max(0,k)\le m\le n+1$, is finite type over $A$. The base is $C_{-1,m}=B$. At stage $k\ge0$, the diagonal case $m=k$ is $P_k$, finite type by hypothesis. If $m>k$, use the cartesian description of step 4 and apply [lem-sfb-finite-type-surjective-product-pullback] with $R=A$, $Q=C_{k-1,m}$, $C_E=P_k$ and $D_E=C_{k-1,k}=M_k(P)$. The index set consists of the finitely many injections $[k]\hookrightarrow[m]$. Both $Q$ and $D_E$ are finite type by the preceding induction stage, and $P_k$ is finite type by hypothesis. Every $\varphi_E=\mu_k$ is surjective by the item hypothesis, and every $\psi_E$ is surjective by step 3. The base $A$ is Noetherian. The cited node therefore gives precisely the required finite type of $C_{k,m}$.

source.place: Tag 08PW (lemma-polynomial), proof: compatible families on skeleta and the cartesian square for successive skeleta.

proof.text: Taking $k=n$ and $m=n+1$ gives a finite type algebra $C_{n,n+1}$. The facet identification of step 2 identifies it with $M_{n+1}(P)$ as an $A$-algebra, proving the assertion. For $n=0$ this is exactly $P_0\times_B P_0$, obtained already by the $k=0,m=1$ induction step.
